SECTION 2641 REIMBURSEMENT FOR COMMUNITY CONTRIBUTIONS TO EDUCATION OR TRAINING — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Morgan Casey Lee

DECLARATION OF PARTIES AND PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This Family Code Section 2641 Reimbursement Information Sheet concerns Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee, whose marital dissolution or legal separation proceeding is pending, or may be filed, in the California superior court for Sacramento County. It describes what California Family Code section 2641 says about the community's right, upon dissolution of marriage or legal separation, to reimbursement for community or quasi-community property spent on the education or training of one party where that education or training substantially enhanced that party's earning capacity. Section 2641 addresses a different reimbursement mechanism than Family Code section 2640, which is the subject of a separate information sheet in this set: section 2640 concerns a spouse's SEPARATE property contributions to the ACQUISITION of COMMUNITY property (for example, a down payment on a house), while section 2641 concerns COMMUNITY contributions to one party's EDUCATION OR TRAINING. This information sheet states what the Family Code says about the section 2641 reimbursement right in general terms. It does not determine, calculate, or assert that the right applies to Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee's specific payments, education, or training, whether any statutory ground for reduction or presumption applies to their specific facts, or whether an express written agreement to the contrary exists between them; those are matters for the court to decide based on the specific facts, or for Jordan Alex Lee and Morgan Casey Lee to resolve by their own written agreement.

WHAT COUNTS AS "COMMUNITY CONTRIBUTIONS TO EDUCATION OR TRAINING" UNDER SECTION 2641
Family Code section 2641 defines "community contributions to education or training," as the term is used in that section, to mean payments made with community or quasi-community property for education or training, or for the repayment of a loan incurred for education or training. By the statute's own terms, this definition applies whether the payments were made while the parties were resident in California or resident outside California. This definition is distinct from, and should not be confused with, Family Code section 2640's separate definition of "contributions to the acquisition of property" (down payments, improvements, and loan-principal payments toward acquiring community property), which is addressed in this corpus's companion Section 2640 Reimbursement Information Sheet and is not restated here.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Community contributions to education or training” as used in this section means payments made with community or quasi-community property for education or training or for the repayment of a loan incurred for education or training, whether the payments were made while the parties were resident in this state or resident outside this state."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(a) (California Legislative Information text), the statute's own definition of "community contributions to education or training" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2641(a), the Legislature's own definitional subdivision, fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2641, cited by this document's other authority clauses (which quote subdivisions (b), (c), (d), and (e)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. The statute's own text does not define "quasi-community property" within section 2641 itself (that term is defined elsewhere in the Family Code), and this document does not address that separate definition. This document also does not address how a party establishes, as an evidentiary matter, that a particular historical payment was made with community or quasi-community property rather than separate property, which the statute's text does not itself resolve.

THE COMMUNITY'S RIGHT TO REIMBURSEMENT WITH INTEREST, AND THE ASSIGNMENT OF RELATED LOANS
Family Code section 2641 provides that, upon dissolution of marriage or legal separation, subject to the limitations stated elsewhere in the statute, the community shall be reimbursed for community contributions to education or training of a party that substantially enhances the earning capacity of that party. This reimbursement is with interest: the statute specifies that the amount reimbursed shall be with interest at the legal rate, accruing from the end of the calendar year in which the contributions were made. Separately, the statute addresses a loan incurred during the marriage for a party's education or training: such a loan is not included among the community's liabilities for purposes of dividing the community estate, but is instead assigned for payment by the party whose education or training the loan financed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The community shall be reimbursed for community contributions to education or training of a party that substantially enhances the earning capacity of the party. The amount reimbursed shall be with interest at the legal rate, accruing from the end of the calendar year in which the contributions were made."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(b)(1) (California Legislative Information text), the core reimbursement right, stated with interest at the legal rate accruing from the end of the calendar year of contribution (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  "A loan incurred during marriage for the education or training of a party shall not be included among the liabilities of the community for the purpose of division pursuant to this division but shall be assigned for payment by the party."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(b)(2) (California Legislative Information text), the rule assigning an education- or training-related loan to the party rather than treating it as a community liability (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2641(b), fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2641, cited by this document's other authority clauses (subdivisions (a), (c), (d), and (e)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. This section 2641(b) reimbursement (with interest at the legal rate) is a materially different formula than Family Code section 2640(b)'s reimbursement (without interest or adjustment for value change, capped at net value at division), which is addressed in this corpus's companion Section 2640 Reimbursement Information Sheet; this document does not restate that separate formula and takes no position on how the two compare beyond noting they are different statutory mechanisms. The statute's own text does not define "the legal rate" numerically within section 2641, nor does it define "substantially enhances the earning capacity," and this document does not address either further. The reimbursement described in this clause is itself subject to the reduction or modification grounds and the ten-year presumption addressed in this document's companion clauses, and to the express-written-agreement exception addressed in another companion clause — this clause states only the core right and the loan-assignment rule, not those qualifications.

REDUCTION FOR UNJUST CIRCUMSTANCES AND THE TEN-YEAR REBUTTABLE PRESUMPTION
Family Code section 2641 states that the reimbursement and assignment the statute otherwise requires shall be reduced or modified to the extent circumstances render that disposition unjust, and lists specific circumstances — stated by the statute to be a non-exhaustive list — that can support such a reduction. One listed circumstance is that the community has substantially benefited from the education, training, or loan incurred for the education or training of the party. The statute attaches a rebuttable presumption, affecting the burden of proof, to the timing of the community's contributions relative to when the dissolution or legal separation proceeding commenced, and the presumption runs in different directions depending on that timing: contributions made LESS than 10 years before commencement of the proceeding are presumed NOT to have substantially benefited the community, while contributions made MORE than 10 years before commencement of the proceeding are presumed TO HAVE substantially benefited the community. Because the statute states this is a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof, rather than a conclusive rule, its own text does not make either directional presumption automatically decide whether reimbursement is reduced in a given case.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The reimbursement and assignment required by this section shall be reduced or modified to the extent circumstances render such a disposition unjust, including, but not limited to, any of the following: (1) The community has substantially benefited from the education, training, or loan incurred for the education or training of the party. There is a rebuttable presumption, affecting the burden of proof, that the community has not substantially benefited from community contributions to the education or training made less than 10 years before the commencement of the proceeding, and that the community has substantially benefited from community contributions to the education or training made more than 10 years before the commencement of the proceeding."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(c), (c)(1) (California Legislative Information text), the reduce-or-modify-if-unjust standard and its non-exhaustive list, and the ten-year rebuttable presumption on whether the community has substantially benefited (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2641(c) and its first listed circumstance, subdivision (c)(1), fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2641, cited by this document's other authority clauses (subdivisions (a), (b), (d), and (e)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. The introductory sentence quoted here ("The reimbursement and assignment required by this section shall be reduced or modified to the extent circumstances render such a disposition unjust, including, but not limited to, any of the following:") also governs the two additional statutory grounds addressed in this document's companion clause on other reduction grounds, subdivisions (c)(2) and (c)(3) — that companion clause is likewise not independent of this one; both quote language from the same subdivision (c). The statute's own text does not specify what evidence or procedure rebuts either directional presumption, nor does it define "commencement of the proceeding" within section 2641 itself, and this document does not address either further. This clause states only the statute's substantial-benefit ground and its associated ten-year presumption; it does not state whether or how that presumption has been applied to any particular set of facts, which is a matter for the court.

OTHER STATUTORY GROUNDS FOR REDUCING OR MODIFYING REIMBURSEMENT
In addition to the community's substantial benefit from the education or training addressed in this document's companion clause, Family Code section 2641 lists two further circumstances that can support reducing or modifying the reimbursement and assignment the statute otherwise requires. First, the statute lists as a ground for reduction that the education or training received by the party is offset by the education or training received by the other party for which community contributions have been made. Second, the statute lists as a ground for reduction that the education or training enables the party who received it to engage in gainful employment that substantially reduces the need of that party for support that would otherwise be required. As with the substantial-benefit ground, the statute's own text states its list of circumstances is not exhaustive.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The education or training received by the party is offset by the education or training received by the other party for which community contributions have been made."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(c)(2) (California Legislative Information text), the offsetting-education ground for reduction (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  "The education or training enables the party receiving the education or training to engage in gainful employment that substantially reduces the need of the party for support that would otherwise be required."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(c)(3) (California Legislative Information text), the reduced-need-for-support ground for reduction (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2641(c)(2) and (c)(3), fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2641, cited by this document's other authority clauses (subdivisions (a), (b), (c)(1), (d), and (e)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. In particular, the introductory sentence governing this clause's two grounds ("reduced or modified to the extent circumstances render such a disposition unjust, including, but not limited to, any of the following") is the same introductory sentence quoted in full in this document's companion clause on the ten-year presumption, subdivision (c)(1); the two clauses are not independent of each other. The statute's own text does not define "offset," "gainful employment," or how "substantially reduces the need" is measured, and this document does not address any of those terms further. This clause does not restate or analyze Family Code section 4320's spousal support factors, addressed in this document's companion clause on exclusivity and in this corpus's Marital Settlement Agreement document.

EXCLUSIVE REMEDY, RELATIONSHIP TO SPOUSAL SUPPORT, AND WAIVER BY WRITTEN AGREEMENT
Family Code section 2641 states that reimbursement for community contributions and assignment of loans under this section is the exclusive remedy of the community or a party for the education or training and any resulting enhancement of the earning capacity of a party — meaning the statute does not provide the community, or either party, with a separate or additional remedy for that same education, training, or earning-capacity enhancement outside of this reimbursement and assignment mechanism. The statute's own text qualifies that exclusivity in one respect: it states that nothing in that subdivision limits consideration of the effect of the education, training, or enhancement, or the amount reimbursed under section 2641, on the circumstances of the parties for purposes of a spousal support order under Family Code section 4320 — a separate statute governing spousal support factors, addressed in this corpus's Marital Settlement Agreement document and not restated here. Finally, section 2641 states that the entire section is subject to an express written agreement of the parties to the contrary.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Reimbursement for community contributions and assignment of loans pursuant to this section is the exclusive remedy of the community or a party for the education or training and any resulting enhancement of the earning capacity of a party. However, nothing in this subdivision limits consideration of the effect of the education, training, or enhancement, or the amount reimbursed pursuant to this section, on the circumstances of the parties for the purpose of an order for support pursuant to Section 4320."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(d) (California Legislative Information text), the exclusive-remedy rule and its cross-reference to spousal support under Section 4320 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  "This section is subject to an express written agreement of the parties to the contrary."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 2641(e) (California Legislative Information text), the express-written-agreement exception to the entire section (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=2641.)
  Known gap: This is the actual text of Family Code section 2641(d) and (e), fetched directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and confirmed byte-identical across two fetches made with different User-Agent strings. This citation is to the same statutory section, 2641, cited by this document's other authority clauses (subdivisions (a), (b), and (c)) — they are not independent of one another; all are different subdivisions of one enacted section. This document does not restate or analyze Family Code section 4320's spousal support factors, which that document's companion Marital Settlement Agreement clause on spousal support factors addresses separately; this clause states only that section 2641(d) cross-references section 4320 for that limited purpose. The statute's own text does not specify what form or language an "express written agreement of the parties to the contrary" under subdivision (e) must take beyond being express and written, and this document does not address that question further.

SIGNATURE AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT — NOT A COURT FILING
